subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status report live gateway runtime health, use a passive local plugin status contract, or remain intentionally inconclusive outside `--all` local probing?
rationale: The current code avoids the old fast-status wording but does not settle the product/API contract for plugin memory health, and the open closing PR conflicts with the broader side-effect issue.

options.title: Adopt live gateway runtime health
options.body: Replace or repair the open fork PR with an explicit runtime-health field in the gateway doctor/status contract and use it in human and JSON status.

options.title: Define passive local plugin status
options.body: Keep status read-only by adding a passive plugin-owned status contract and avoid local heavyweight manager startup.

options.title: Keep current inconclusive status
options.body: Close the conflicting PR and accept `not checked` as the supported output unless a user opts into local probing.

recommendation.title: Adopt live gateway runtime health
recommendation.body: Replace or repair the open fork PR with an explicit runtime-health field in the gateway doctor/status contract and use it in human and JSON status.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on both the plugin-routed memory runtime and the custom memory status surface.
